answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a tiered identity bond. To join, each agent locks a stake of sable into a bonded terrace; the top terrace demands exponentially more sable, so minting thousands of fake identities costs real capital the attacker cannot reclaim. A public randomness beacon picks which agents get audited each epoch, and dishonest attestations slash the bond. Because that beacon is unpredictable, a Sybil farmer cannot dodge checks, and the locked sable turns every extra identity into a non-recoverable expense rather than a free account.
